public_rationale: Microsoft reported $34.9 billion in capital expenditure for July–September 2025, covering cloud and AI together; this does not establish cumulative AI-only spending [e1]. Alphabet reported a 30.5% consolidated operating margin for the same quarter, which does not establish AI-attributable profit [e2]. These disclosures neither establish nor disprove the assertion that the four companies had earned no AI profit [e1, e2]. They also do not verify approximately $605 billion in cumulative AI capex or the two-to-one revenue requirement used to derive $1.21 trillion [e1, e2].
limitations: The evidence lacks comparable AI-specific revenue and attributable costs for all four companies; missing disclosure does not establish zero profit.
The cumulative spending window, AI allocation and investment-recovery assumptions are not established.
The evidence does not settle whether $1.21 trillion denotes a gross revenue requirement or a remaining shortfall after revenue already earned.
Positive profit in a reporting period would not by itself establish recovery of cumulative investment.

our_interpretation: Profit means profit attributable to the AI activities discussed, after their attributable costs. Consolidated company profit does not settle this assertion.
The passage also concerns recovery of cumulative AI investment. Positive profit in a reporting period and recovery of all historical investment are separate tests.

The $1.21 trillion figure is an estimated revenue requirement derived from the speaker's capex estimate and multiplier. 'Hole' could mean either that gross requirement or the remaining shortfall after revenue already earned; neither meaning is imposed exclusively.
The cumulative observation extends through an unspecified calculation date no later than the post. Its starting date is unknown. December 8 is an outer boundary, not an asserted calculation date.

For the ongoing profitability component, the latest reported quarter before publication is the quarter ended September 30, 2025. That quarter is not substituted for the unspecified cumulative capex period.
The metric scope records the estimated revenue requirement. The accompanying profit assertion has no stated accounting basis.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish the relevant cumulative AI capex at approximately $605 billion, substantiate the two-to-one revenue requirement, and show no positive AI-attributable profit for the four companies over the period asserted. If 'hole' means a remaining shortfall, the calculation must also account for revenue already earned.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish positive AI-attributable profit for a named company during the asserted period, or materially disprove the cumulative capex or revenue-requirement calculation. Company-wide profits, broad cloud profits, and positive revenue alone are insufficient. Evidence about a residual shortfall cannot by itself disprove a gross revenue requirement.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated AI-attributable revenue and cost records for the four companies over the asserted period, plus a reconciliation of the approximately $605 billion capex estimate and a verified model for the two-to-one revenue requirement. The records must identify the spending and recovery periods, allocate shared infrastructure and leases consistently, and account for revenue already earned if $1.21 trillion denotes a remaining shortfall.
